sources.entry: KnockKnock - See what's persistently installed on your Mac. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/objective-see/KnockKnock)

summary.name: KnockKnock
summary.one_liner: KnockKnock is a free macOS tool from Objective-See that scans for software set to start automatically (persistence) and lists it so you can spot possible malware.
use_cases: Finding software that launches automatically on a Mac
Checking a Mac for persistent malware
Reviewing login items, launch agents and daemons
Scheduled command-line scans of persistence locations
Comparing scan results to spot new or changed startup items
summary.what_it_does: KnockKnock enumerates known macOS locations where software can be installed to start automatically, including launch items, login items, browser extensions, cron jobs, shell configuration files, and many other categories. Each detected item shows its signing status (Apple, third-party signed, or unsigned), path, and info or Finder buttons. If VirusTotal integration is enabled, it queries VirusTotal by binary hash and flags known malware in red. Scans can be saved as JSON and compared against a previous scan, with new, removed and modified items marked. A command-line mode allows scheduled or elevated (sudo) scans.
notable: Covers many persistence categories, from launch items and login items to kernel extensions and shell config files
Optional VirusTotal hash lookup and submission, with known malware highlighted
Command-line interface for scripted or sudo-elevated scans, with JSON output
Compare feature marks new (+), removed (-) and modified (~) items between scans
caveats: Lists legitimate third-party software too; it does not classify items as malicious by itself
Needs Full Disk Access granted in System Settings for a complete scan
Signed Apple items are filtered out by default; a VirusTotal API key is needed for malware lookups
